message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**What the 10-K showed (FY ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024):**
- **Net income: $93,736 million** (down from $96,995M in FY2023) — the decline was driven almost entirely by a **one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge** related to the European Commission's State Aid Decision (Ireland), which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7%.
- Total net sales: $391,035M (+2% YoY), with Services up 13% to $96,169M and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%.
- Operating income: $123,216M (up from $114,301M), and cash generated by operating activities of $118,254M — so the underlying operating business actually improved; the earnings dip is a non-recurring tax item, not operational deterioration.
- Balance sheet remains very strong: $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities, plus $95.0B returned via buybacks and $15.2B in dividends during the year.

**What I did:** With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for **44 shares at $222.75** — a limit essentially at the current market price, which filled at $222.75 for a total of **$9,801.00**. That is within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, uses only existing cash ($50,000 available, no money moved out of the account), and is a buy in an in-mandate name (AAPL). I did not touch the existing 100 MSFT shares. Rationale: record revenue, expanding gross margins, and rising operating income and operating cash flow, with the reported net income decline attributable to a disclosed one-time tax charge rather than a weakening franchise — a favorable setup for a modest, mandate-compliant add.
